text:
emma (oncall): Alert: KMS decrypt spike detected for service-account 'ingest-worker@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' in prod-us-west-2 — ~120 decrypts in last 3m. Creating incident room.

sanjay (sec eng): Ack. Pulling KMS audit logs and recent IAM/API logs.

maria (infra): On it — checking terraform/apply history and recent RBAC changes.

deploy-bot: notice: terraform apply by deployer-ci@ci (run-id: r-8f3a) completed 2025-10-23T14:02:11Z. Changes: +google_service_account_iam_binding.ingest_worker: role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"

emma (oncall): If that binding is new, treat as possible misconfiguration or escalation path. Sanjay — can you confirm whether decrypt targets are only internal KMS keys or external? :eyes:

sanjay (sec eng): Keys targeted are customer-data-encrypt-prod (KMS key id: kms-01a2). Decrypt callers are all from the same SA and some external IPs show TCP connections shortly after. Collecting IPs and pod names.

maria (infra): I see the TF diff. Here's the snippet:
```
resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "ingest_worker" {
  service_account_id = "ingest-worker@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  role               = "roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
}
```
This was added in the commit referenced by deployer-ci.

emma (oncall): Assigning roles: sanjay = incident commander, maria = ops lead. I'll take comms + timeline. Containment options: remove binding, rotate SA keys, restrict network egress from pods using SA.

sanjay (sec eng): Recommend immediate removal of the binding and rotate any long-lived credentials. KMS key rotation isn't instant; rely on SA revocation. I'll prepare an audit snapshot and indicators of compromise.

maria (infra): Applied binding removal at 2025-10-23T14:15:03Z — verified with iam.getBinding. Also applied a NetworkPolicy to block egress from pods with label app=ingest-worker. Confirming decrypts stopped at 2025-10-23T14:18:20Z per KMS audit logs.

emma (oncall): Good. Evidence steps: (1) export KMS audit logs to secure-bucket redwood-incidents/kms/1765432107/ (2) snapshot TF state and commit diff (3) capture pod images and container digests. Opening internal ticket INF-7890 and attaching artifacts.

sanjay (sec eng): I'll run quick binary checks, look for suspicious startup commands, and search for large outbound transfers. If we see exfil, escalate to CISO and legal.

maria (infra): No obvious exfil in volumes; some outbound to 18.203.45.12 over 443 — flagged for review.

emma (oncall): Handoff: Jordan will take on-call at 17:00 UTC. Jordan, summary and pending tasks:
- Validate KMS log export in secure-bucket
- Continue IP investigation (18.203.45.12)
- Run post-incident RBAC audit for related service accounts
- Coordinate next steps for rotating any remaining credentials

jordan (oncall-next): Ack. I'll pick this up at shift change and confirm artifacts + follow-ups in INF-7890. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

emma (oncall): Closing war-room active ops. Will post final timeline and remediation steps in ticket by EOD.
